name: Nigeria
headline: Nigeria: +4.0% growth in 2025, 23.0% inflation, debt 36% of GDP
sections: Nigeria is a $290 billion economy (2025), the world's 51st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.0% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $9,532 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.3% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 23.0% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, up from 18.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.1% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 5.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 36% of GDP (2025), a low level that has risen from 26% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.8% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +4.8% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Net FDI inflows were 1.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 32% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 54.6 years (2024). Population: 237.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
